As a metaphor for brain function, the movie was highly problematic. Mostly accuracy was sacrificed for the plot and to keep the movie simple and entertaining. However, it is a very interesting thought experiment – how to design a metaphor that accurately captures brain function according to our best current knowledge. I do hope the movie motivates people to think about brain function, but I fear it will increase some poor brain metaphors in the public consciousness.

I'd love if someone pulled that off. It would be a fantastically useful abstraction, to the point where we could develop a modern functioning symbolic pantheon, of sorts. Joseph Campbell would dance in his grave.

My standard for science appearing in a fictional setting is merely that it is plausible.

I would rate Robert Heinlein very highly because he always wrote things that were for the most part highly plausible.

I think it is most important that each brain have a highly plausible and richly developed metaphor for each scientific and philosophical concept.

It is of lesser importance, the degree of absolute accuracy in any individual brain, so long as those with the most accurate conceptions are allowed to act freely in the agora of ideas.

In the long run, those with the best brain metaphors will out-compete those with poor models of reality in the greater public consciousness. Or at least my brain is telling me this is so right now based on its core and most recent working memories. (look, I used the model in the movie, for better or for worse.)

Sounds right to me. When describing "best" brain metaphors - the qualities of flexibility and ability to combine ideas in original ways will likely be the most advantageous. The metaphors locked into predictable states will lock the individual into more predictable outcomes - for better or worse.

I'm 50-something myself. Here's what I know.

There are basically three kinds of vapes, the kind that use ground bud (flower), the kind that use extracts (oil or wax) and the kind that use the cartridges, like e-cigs do. The third kind pretty much requires that you live in a legal state, or have access to someone who does.

Oils and wax are something you can make at home (butane extraction is one common method, not hard, but for god's sake do it outside or you'll blow the house up). You might be able to make the liquid for the cartridges at home but I don't know anything about that.

Flower vapes have existed of a long time, but of course that are much nicer these days. They come in portable and desktop models, the desktop version being superior in every respect except for portability. The resulting vapor is dry and benefits greatly from being run through a water pipe.

My only direct experience is with two flower vapes, a lighter-powered portable (the Vaporgenie, which works OK but is fussy) and an Epic e-nano desktop, which I run through a water pipe and which is fucking amazing. The leftover flower still have active ingredients and can be eaten or mixed into food without further processing, for an additional high.

The most common vapes are where you grind up the weed and put it in that and take hits. A good entry level vape is the Flowermate v.05, check out some youtube videos about it. Also this guy's website is cool once you get your feet wet: http://www.vapecritic.com/

Also 50ish! I've been vaping for about 5 years....tried different models, and the technology is evolving fast. Currently, I use something called a Pax...a little electrically charged cylinder that you pack about .3 gram of finely ground/powdered weed into and recharge after every couple of uses. I clean mine...mostly the filter part...after every 8 uses or so...I really like it...portable, rugged, and you decrease the stink you subject your household to by about 98%

Hey, I've got a few vapes. Maybe I can help.

You're either working with Bud or Extract. Maybe infused E-Juice...but that's not a great option. Vaping is simply heating up the trichomes until they boil off and vaporize. You then suck that up. The bud doesn't burn and can be used again in cooking (much less potent than fresh bud)

BUD VAPES

Desktop vapes. I have an Silver Surfer, a power ceramic heater based vape. I keep it on for most of the day, I run it through a bong. It gives big hits, very efficient. Keep my lungs feeling healthy. I use it every day.

Portable Vapes. I've had a Pax, it wasn't efficient. It did give big clouds, but started to smell like fart after 6 months. No amount of cleaning will rid the vape of the smell. Worked really well other than that.

My mate just bought a Stores and Bickel Mighty. It was fucking expensive, it is AMAZING. Lasts 8 bowls or so. Very accurate temp reading, digital. Awesomeness

EXTRACTS

I got my extract vape pen about a month ago. I live in Australia, so no dispensaries here. I make my extracts with Iso Alcohol. This is the future of portable vaping. I've got a Gentlesman Vape with a Mega Cart. I can put 1g of extract in and it will last a number of people for a night.

So why vape?

The taste, bongs taste like crap now. I can tell the taste difference between weeds. Kinda cool and unexpected plus side.

Efficient, my usage dropped by 2/3. Bit of a different high, maybe that's why.
